title: In-browser Pyodide runner: run examples + grade exercises client-side (lazy-load, offline fallback)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The in-browser runner is the project's headline user-facing feature: zero install, zero account, instant correct feedback. It runs entirely client-side via Pyodide (Python WASM), so no learner code ever reaches a server. The runner must be accessible (keyboard/AT usable) as a precondition for the M2 site build.
objective: Build the in-browser Pyodide-based runner that lets learners run runnable examples and submit exercises for client-side grading, with lazy-loading, service-worker caching, and a graceful offline/no-WASM fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: Learner can run any runnable example from a lesson with zero install and zero account; code executes in the browser via Pyodide.
Learner can submit exercise attempts and receive graded feedback (pass/fail, failure details) entirely client-side; learner code never leaves the device.
Grading uses the exercise's test suite; failure messages are actionable (not just 'wrong').
Pyodide runtime is lazy-loaded and cached (service worker or equivalent); subsequent loads do not re-download the full WASM bundle.
A graceful 'download to run locally' fallback exists where WASM is unavailable or blocked.
Runner UI is keyboard-navigable and usable with assistive technology (screen reader, focus order correct, no keyboard traps).
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
output: A merged PR adding the in-browser Pyodide runner component, lazy-load/cache strategy, offline fallback, and accessibility attributes.
